hints.title: Use the given factor
hints.body: Write the cubic as f(x). Since x+2 is a factor, f(−2)=0, which determines a.
hints.recap: Evaluate at the zero of a linear factor.
hints.pause: Substitute <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></math> into all three nonconstant terms.

hints.title: Remove that factor
hints.body: After finding a, divide the cubic by x+2. Start with 3x2, multiply it by x+2 and subtract before finding the next quotient term.
hints.recap: Polynomial division removes a known factor and leaves a lower-degree polynomial.
hints.pitfall: Subtract the full product at each division step.

recall.reminder: Polynomial division removes a known factor and leaves a lower-degree polynomial.

hints.title: Finish the factorisation
hints.body: The quotient is 3x2+7x−6. Seek two factors whose constant product is −6 and whose cross terms total 7x.
hints.recap: A complete cubic factorisation must include all three linear factors.
hints.pitfall: A correct constant product with the wrong middle coefficient is insufficient.
hints.pause: Factor the quadratic and multiply the result by <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></math>.

recall.reminder: A complete cubic factorisation must include all three linear factors.

solution:
The factor theorem gives 3(−2)3+13(−2)2+8(−2)+a=0. This is −24+52−16+a=0, so a=−12.

Dividing 3x3+13x2+8x−12 by x+2 gives 3x2+7x−6. This factors as (x+3)(3x−2), since its cross terms are 9x−2x=7x.

The complete factorisation is therefore (x+2)(x+3)(3x−2), option E. Multiplication gives the original cubic with constant −12.
knowledgePattern: Factor theorem followed by cubic division and quadratic factorisation
